necessaryObstacle: The existing native Gamma0 formula uses level-multiple loops. Multiplication by the level can kill genuine torsion boundary information. The primitive-loop calculation is required to connect the literal H1/parabolic quotient to an arithmetic finite-column operator family.
reuseDecision: Reuse native principal reduction, coset equivalences, unipotent matrices, finite primitive columns and integral Hecke conjugation. Do not add a second modular-symbol carrier, a general open-curve theory or an arbitrary extension of the boundary operators. Adapt only the actual primitive-loop trace needed here.
discharged: Every primitive Gamma1 cusp width divides the original level and is prime to every good Hecke prime.
The actual primitive Hecke action has one fixed coset, all other orbit lengths equal to the Hecke prime, and exactly two cyclic orbits in total.
Independent unit rescaling of the cusp coordinates preserves the primitive width.
Primitive cusp values descend to the existing finite residue-column carrier; its actual homogeneous H1 boundary has exactly parabolic H1 as kernel, including torsion coefficients when two is a unit.
Original Gamma1 conjugation preserves the primitive width, loop and character value.
remaining: Identify both literal diagonal-conjugation orbit terms and prove the two-term primitive Hecke formula.
Construct the corresponding genuine cyclotomic boundary operators and prove the normalized Frobenius relation.

Retain the actual diamond factor in the boundary determinant until the original diamond-one character is proved to descend on the enlarged joint algebra. The current prime-word character alone does not justify dropping this factor.
